judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs sit under Competency C-2.5 (identifying, describing and extending simple number patterns) within CG-2. The Class-4 item (rank 3) is '• Patterns in multiplication (5x10, 5x100, 5x1000)', with LC 'Identify and extend patterns in multiplication when multiplying by 10, 100 and 1000'; the Class-5 item (rank 4) is '• Multiples and common multiples', with LCs 'Identify and find multiples of a given number' and 'Identify common multiples of two numbers'. This is lower-to-higher rank with a substantive extension rather than plain repetition: generating and extending multiplication patterns (repeated products of a given number scaled by powers of ten) supplies the multiplicative-product fluency and pattern-extension habit that identifying multiples of a number, and then common multiples of two numbers, requires. Direction is therefore Class-4 to Class-5 (second_to_first), the only permitted developmental direction. judgment.rationale: The Class-3 Content bullet '• Reading a particular day and date' sits under CG-4/C-4.4 (measurement of time, estimating time) and its LCs are 'Read a particular date from a calendar' and 'Read a particular day from a calendar'. The Class-5 Content bullet 'Angles through clocks and time reading' sits under CG-3/C-3.1 (attributes of 2D/3D shapes) with LCs 'Identify angles formed by the hands of a clock' and 'Read time on a clock'. There is genuine same-topic coherence: both concern reading conventional time instruments, and 'read time on a clock' reinforces the time-reading strand begun with calendar day/date reading. However, the Class-5 item's substantive learning demand is geometric (angles formed by clock hands) and its time-reading is on a clock rather than a calendar, so calendar day/date reading is not shown to support success in the angle/clock work; the developmental link asserted by the nomination rests mainly on the shared token 'reading' plus weak page proximity (gap 1), which is not sufficient for buildsTowards.
